idea: a multiplayer game server in Rust

plan.summary: An authoritative multiplayer game server written in Rust using WebSockets, supporting room-based lobbies (join via room code), real-time message broadcasting, and a simple built-in turn-based game (Tic-Tac-Toe) as a reference implementation of the game logic layer, designed so the game rules module can be swapped out for other games.
stack: tokio-tungstenite based Rust CLI test client (dev tool)

phases.name: Phase 1: Project scaffolding
steps: Initialize a Cargo workspace with two crates: `server` (binary) and `client` (binary, dev/test tool), plus a shared `protocol` library crate for message types.
Add dependencies: tokio (full features), tokio-tungstenite, futures-util, serde, serde_json, dashmap, uuid (v4), tracing, tracing-subscriber, clap (derive), anyhow/thiserror for error handling.
Set up tracing_subscriber initialization and a `--port` / `--host` CLI flag via clap for the server binary.

Define the `protocol` crate with serde-serializable enums: ClientMessage (Join{room_code, player_name}, CreateRoom{player_name}, MakeMove{payload}, Chat{text}, Leave) and ServerMessage (RoomCreated{room_code}, RoomJoined{room_id, players}, PlayerJoined, PlayerLeft, GameState{...}, GameOver{winner}, Chat, Error{message}).

phases.name: Phase 2: Connection & session management
steps: Implement a Tokio TCP listener wrapped by tokio-tungstenite to accept WebSocket upgrades on the configured port.
On each new connection, spawn an async task that splits the WebSocket into sink/stream halves; create a Player struct (id: Uuid, name, sender channel to write half).
Implement a central `AppState` shared via Arc containing a DashMap<RoomCode, Room> and DashMap<PlayerId, mpsc::UnboundedSender<ServerMessage>> for outbound routing.

Implement message read loop per connection: deserialize incoming JSON text frames into ClientMessage, dispatch to a room/session handler; handle WebSocket ping/pong and close frames; on disconnect, remove player from room and broadcast PlayerLeft.
Implement graceful error handling: malformed messages return a ServerMessage::Error to the sender without killing the connection.

phases.name: Phase 3: Room/lobby system
steps: Implement Room struct: room_code (short random alphanumeric, e.g. 6 chars via uuid or a custom generator), list of up to 2 players (for tic-tac-toe), game state enum (Waiting, InProgress, Finished), and a broadcast channel for room-wide messages.
Implement CreateRoom handler: generate unique room code, insert into DashMap, add creator as player 1, send RoomCreated back to creator.

Implement Join handler: look up room by code, reject if full or nonexistent (send Error), otherwise add player, broadcast PlayerJoined to all room members, and once 2 players present transition room state to InProgress and send initial GameState.

Implement Leave/disconnect handling: remove player from room; if room becomes empty, remove it from DashMap after a short delay; if a player leaves mid-game, broadcast GameOver{winner: remaining_player} to the other player.
Add a room reaper background task (tokio::spawn with interval) that cleans up empty or stale rooms periodically.

phases.name: Phase 4: Game logic (Tic-Tac-Toe reference implementation)
steps: Define a `GameLogic` trait with methods: new_game(), apply_move(player_id, move_payload) -> Result<MoveOutcome, GameError>, current_state() -> serializable state, is_over() -> Option<GameResult>. This isolates game rules from networking so other games can be plugged in later.
Implement TicTacToe struct implementing GameLogic: 3x3 board array, turn tracking, move validation (cell empty, correct player's turn), win/draw detection after each move.
Wire MakeMove client messages through Room -> GameLogic::apply_move; on success broadcast updated GameState to both players; on game over broadcast GameOver{winner or draw} and mark room Finished.
Add rejection of moves from spectators, out-of-turn players, or after game has ended, returning ServerMessage::Error.

phases.name: Phase 5: Chat & misc features
steps: Implement Chat message relay: any player message broadcast to all other players in the same room with sender name attached.
Add a heartbeat/ping mechanism: server sends WebSocket ping every 30s and disconnects clients that don't respond within a timeout window.
Add basic rate limiting per connection (e.g. max N messages per second) to prevent flooding, dropping or warning on excess.

phases.name: Phase 6: Test client & manual testing tools
steps: Implement the `client` binary: connects via tokio-tungstenite to a given server URL, reads stdin lines, parses simple commands (`create <name>`, `join <code> <name>`, `move <row> <col>`, `chat <text>`, `leave`), sends corresponding ClientMessage JSON, and prints incoming ServerMessage events to stdout.

Add an integration test in `server/tests/` that spins up the server on a random port in-process, connects two mock WebSocket clients via tokio-tungstenite, plays a full tic-tac-toe game to completion, and asserts correct GameOver message.

phases.name: Phase 7: Concurrency, robustness & polish
steps: Review all shared-state access paths for lock contention/deadlocks; ensure DashMap entry APIs are used correctly to avoid holding locks across await points.
Add graceful shutdown handling: listen for SIGINT/SIGTERM (tokio::signal), notify all connected clients with a Shutdown ServerMessage, close connections cleanly.
Add configurable limits via CLI flags: max concurrent rooms, max players per room, idle timeout duration.
Write unit tests for TicTacToe win/draw detection covering all win lines and edge cases.
Add `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt` passes; fix warnings.
Write top-level README with build/run instructions (`cargo run -p server -- --port 8080`), architecture overview diagram in text, and how to extend with a new game via the GameLogic trait.
